proposals.before: In the fourth year of the Daming era of Song (460), he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sao was also well known and had already taken the provincial nomination in an earlier year. The Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai then wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and its people may truly be said to have found the right men."
proposals.after: In the fourth year of the Daming era of Song (460), he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. The Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai then wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and its people may truly be said to have found the right men."
proposals.reason: 璲 is Sui, not Sao; the English given name is a romanization error.

proposals.before: The emperor wished to appoint Huan Secretariat Gentleman and had Minister of Officials He Jian convey his intent.
proposals.after: The emperor wished to appoint Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had Minister of Officials He Ji convey his intent.
proposals.reason: 何戢 is He Ji (戢 jí), not He Jian; English also omits as before the office.

proposals.before: The Emperor wished to employ Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had the Minister of the Ministry of Officials He Jian convey his intent.
proposals.after: The Emperor wished to employ Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had the Minister of the Ministry of Officials He Ji convey his intent.
proposals.reason: 何戢 is He Ji, not He Jian.

proposals.before: Jian said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Secretariat—the Phoenix Pool—but regrets that your seniority is still slight. You may accept the previous appointment for the moment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and the higher post will follow immediately thereafter."
proposals.after: Ji said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Secretariat—the Phoenix Pool—but regrets that your seniority is still slight. You may accept the previous appointment for the moment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and the higher post will follow immediately thereafter."
proposals.reason: Shortened given name of 戢 should be Ji.

proposals.before: Jian said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Phoenix Pool; he regrets that your qualifications are light. You may for the moment accept the previous appointment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and then the later post will be conferred at once."
proposals.after: Ji said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Phoenix Pool; he regrets that your qualifications are light. You may for the moment accept the previous appointment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and then the later post will be conferred at once."
proposals.reason: Shortened given name of 戢 should be Ji.

proposals.before: Jin, styled Zijun.
proposals.after: Jin, styled Zijing.
proposals.reason: Courtesy name 子璥 is Zǐjǐng (璥), not Zijun.

proposals.before: He matched the square track and was upright.
proposals.after: He was regular and upright in conduct.
proposals.reason: 方軌 is an idiom for keeping to the proper path, not a literal square track.

proposals.before: Before he could move in he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to conduct the fast at Huan's house.
proposals.after: Before he could move in he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to take Ye to conduct the fast at Huan's house.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 將曅 is omitted in the English; 曅 is a personal name in this chapter (武陵王曅).

proposals.before: [=] Jin, styled Zijun.
proposals.after: [=] Jin, styled Zijing.
proposals.reason: Courtesy name 子璥 is Zǐjǐng, not Zijun.

proposals.before: Before he could move his residence he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to lead the fast at Huan's house.
proposals.after: Before he could move his residence he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to take Ye to lead the fast at Huan's house.
proposals.reason: Chinese 將曅 is omitted; 曅 is a personal name later identified as the Prince of Wuling.

proposals.before: At the beginning of the Taishi era of Song, he served as Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing; in deliberations on the empress's taboo name and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
proposals.after: At the beginning of the Taishi era of Song, he served as Gentleman of the Palace Hall in the Masters of Writing; in deliberations on the empress's taboo name and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
proposals.reason: 殿中郎 is a Masters of Writing gentleman post, not 侍中 (Palace Attendant).

proposals.before: At the beginning of Taishi of Song, he became Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing; in discussing the taboo name of the empress and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Taishi of Song, he became Gentleman of the Palace Hall in the Masters of Writing; in discussing the taboo name of the empress and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 殿中郎 as Palace Attendant.

proposals.before: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's argument that the empress does not use her surname, and that in the Spring and Autumn Annals the queen was moved against to Qi. Cheng failed to cite clear classical evidence and instead based his position on personal opinion; for this he was dismissed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
proposals.after: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's argument that the empress does not use her surname, and that in the Spring and Autumn Annals the queen was met and escorted from Qi. Cheng failed to cite clear classical evidence and instead based his position on personal opinion; for this he was dismissed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
proposals.reason: 逆王后于齊 is the classic 'go to meet the queen in Qi', not military 'moved against'.

proposals.before: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's discussion that the empress does not use her surname, and that in Spring and Autumn the queen was moved against to Qi. Cheng did not cite classic evidence clearly but established the discussion by personal opinion; on this account he was removed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
proposals.after: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's discussion that the empress does not use her surname, and that in Spring and Autumn the queen was met and escorted from Qi. Cheng did not cite classic evidence clearly but established the discussion by personal opinion; on this account he was removed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 逆 as hostile movement.

proposals.before: Zhou was called the old statutes; Han spoke of precedents. From the He and Luo down to the Huai and sea, the court's laws and measures always looked to prior standards.
proposals.after: The Zhou spoke of old statutes; the Han spoke of precedents. From the He and Luo down to the Huai and sea, the court's laws and measures always looked to prior standards.
proposals.reason: 周稱舊章 means Zhou invoked old statutes, not that Zhou 'was called' the old statutes.

proposals.before: Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xin directly, also stating that he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
proposals.after: Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xinshi directly, also stating that he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
proposals.reason: Chinese 孔欣時 is Kong Xinshi; Kong Xin drops 時.

proposals.before: Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xin directly. It also said he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
proposals.after: Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xinshi directly. It also said he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
proposals.reason: Same truncation of 孔欣時.

proposals.before: Mi's impeachment came after the present niche; the matter proceeded under sagely illumination.
proposals.after: Mi's impeachment came after the present accession; the matter proceeded under sagely illumination.
proposals.reason: 今龕 is not a 'niche'; the idiomatic 'present reign/accession' matches the political sense.

proposals.before: Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was bound and dismissed.
proposals.after: Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was accordingly dismissed.
proposals.reason: 結免 means dismissal as the conclusion of the case, not that Zhang Yong was physically bound.

proposals.before: Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was bound and removed.
proposals.after: Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was accordingly removed from office.
proposals.reason: 結免 is consequential dismissal, not binding with ropes.

proposals.before: The following year he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Officials.
proposals.after: The following year he was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Attendant, not Attendant Within the Yellow Gates (黃門侍郎).

proposals.before: The next year he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Officials.
proposals.after: The next year he was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is mistranslated as a Yellow Gates office.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese lists 散騎常侍 and 祕書監 as two offices; the idiomatic English fuses them into one Palace Library title.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise merges 散騎常侍 with 祕書監, which are distinct posts.

proposals.before: He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, retaining his post as rectifier.
proposals.after: He was additionally made Attendant for Affairs, retaining his post as rectifier.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is not the Yellow Gates office (黃門); the English title is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, with his rectifier post as before.
proposals.after: He was additionally made Attendant for Affairs, with his rectifier post as before.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is mistranslated as the Yellow Gates office in the literal English as well.

proposals.before: Cheng met Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Wang Daolong on the road and kowtowed until it bled; on this account he was pardoned.
proposals.after: Cheng met Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Wang Daolong on the road and kowtowed until it bled; on this account Xian was pardoned.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 見原 is Xian, whose death sentence is the topic; the literal 'he' wrongly points to Cheng.

proposals.before: Zheng Xuan was born at the end of Han; his teaching was ample and harmonious, the Confucian school of an entire age. Bao and Cheng walked the same path; elders regarded him as a former exemplar, and the young did not dare dissent.
proposals.after: Zheng Xuan was born at the end of Han; his teaching was ample and harmonious, the Confucian school of an entire age. Baocheng walked the same path; elders regarded him as a former exemplar, and the young did not dare dissent.
proposals.reason: 褒成 is a single compound (the Baocheng enfeoffment/tradition), not two personal names Bao and Cheng.

decisions.reason: The given name is 璲, read Suí; Sao is a romanization error, and Sui is the accurate English form.
The literal likewise wrongly renders 璲 as Sao; Sui matches the Chinese given name.
戢 is jí, so 何戢 is He Ji, not He Jian. Adding as before the office is grammatical and does not change the sense of 用瓛爲中書郎.
The literal repeats the same misreading of 何戢 as He Jian; He Ji is required.
The speaker is named 戢; the shortened English given name must be Ji, not Jian.
The literal attribution 戢謂瓛曰 likewise requires Ji rather than Jian.
The courtesy name is 子璥 (Zǐjǐng). Zijun does not match 璥; Zijing is the correct romanization.
方軌正直 is already rendered idiomatically in the idiomatic field. The literal calque matched the square track is a word-for-word reading of 方軌, not a semantic error.
將曅 is omitted from the English. 將 is the verb take/lead and 曅 is a personal name, so restoring take Ye is required by the Chinese.
The literal 字子璥 must be Zijing, not Zijun; 璥 is jǐng.
The literal also drops 將曅. Taking Ye to lead the fast at Huan's house restores the omitted name and the verb 將.
尚書殿中郎 is a gentleman of the palace hall in the Masters of Writing, not 侍中 Palace Attendant.
The literal has the same office error: 殿中郎 is Gentleman of the Palace Hall, not Palace Attendant.
春秋逆王后于齊 uses 逆 in the classic bridal-reception sense go to meet the queen, not a hostile moved against.
The literal repeats the false military reading of 逆王后于齊; met and escorted from Qi matches the Spring and Autumn usage.
周稱舊章 means Zhou invoked or spoke of the old statutes, parallel to 漢言故事; was called the old statutes misreads 稱.
The personal name is the three-character 孔欣時. Kong Xin drops 時; Kong Xinshi is complete.
The literal likewise truncates 孔欣時 to Kong Xin; Kong Xinshi restores 時.
今龕 is not a physical niche. In this memorial it marks the present dynastic settlement, so present accession matches 今龕之後 and the idiomatic present reign.
結免 is the case concluded in dismissal, not physical binding. Accordingly dismissed restores the legal sense of 結.
The literal bound and removed similarly mistakes 結 for binding with ropes; 結免 is consequential removal from office.
給事中 is Supervising Attendant, not Attendant Within the Yellow Gates (黃門侍郎). Ministry of Personnel is an accurate rendering of 吏部.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 轉給事中，祕書監，遷吏部

decisions.reason: The literal likewise equates 給事中 with the Yellow Gates office; Supervising Attendant is the correct title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 轉給事中，祕書監，遷吏部

decisions.reason: The Chinese lists 散騎常侍 and 祕書監 as two posts. Regular Attendant at the Palace Library fuses them; the repaired list keeps them distinct.
The literal has the same fusion of 散騎常侍 with 祕書監; they are separate offices.
加給事中 is not the Yellow Gates post. Attendant for Affairs is an accurate English title for 給事中.
The literal repeats the Yellow Gates mistranslation of 給事中; Attendant for Affairs is correct.
鮮…當死 is the topic of 見原. Cheng kowtows; Xian, not Cheng, is the one pardoned. The idiomatic field already names Xian.

decisions.after: Zheng Xuan was born at the end of Han; his teaching was ample and harmonious, the Confucian school of an entire age, running on the same track as Baocheng; elders regarded him as a former exemplar, and the young did not dare dissent.
decisions.reason: 褒成 is one compound, not Bao and Cheng, but the proposal makes Baocheng the walker of 竝軌. The teaching is the subject: it ran on the same track as the Baocheng tradition.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 restores 璲 as Sui; the extracted English given name Sao was produced only by the bad romanization.
Accepted r0003 restores 何戢 as He Ji; the English personal name He Jian followed the mistranslation.
Accepted r0005 restores the shortened given name of 戢 as Ji; Jian was created by the bad English.
Accepted r0022 shows 給事中 is Supervising Attendant; the extracted English office title copied the Yellow Gates mistranslation.
